_comment: C0-13 krea bodies EN. 无附加小节。正文「相关条目」3 行带 .md 链接（ideogram/flux/veo），related 写 3 条。sources 3 条对齐 frontmatter。

axes.model_access: Multi-model aggregation + in-house hybrid: the official site lists 64+ models (Veo/Ideogram/Runway/Luma/Flux/Gemini etc., as seen in the site navigation); the in-house Krea 2 line (named on the official site); a real-time generation line (site copy: "real-time as you type or draw").
axes.runtime: Web (krea.ai); generation on the vendor's cloud. No official offline-weights line seen; the real-time line is latency-sensitive, official copy stresses low latency (no concrete SLA verified).
axes.local_files: Works stored account-side in the cloud; no officially stated local data surface. Whether training artifacts (LoRA) can be exported to local — no clear statement on official pages (unverified).
axes.background: Real-time generation is the selling point (output as you type/draw, official copy); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified).
axes.tools: Real-time canvas, LoRA fine-tuning (official copy), upscaling line (official copy mentions a 22K ceiling; the fetched snapshot did not show that figure — not verified item by item), video-model aggregation (Veo/Runway etc. served through the aggregation surface); an API surface exists, details not verified item by item.
axes.context: Organized by projects/boards (as seen in site navigation); cross-session memory — no official statement verified. The real-time canvas's "current frame" is in-session state, not persistent memory.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription system (D9: prices not collected); training use: official marketing copy claims user content is not used for training ("Do not train"); the privacy-page original wording not verified line by line — marketing talk vs. terms, the original text governs.
axes.fit: Fits: real-time interactive creation (draw-and-see), switching between multiple vendors' models on one platform, LoRA training without a local environment. Does not fit: wanting open weights, offline use, or deep per-model parameter control.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **The real quality-latency curves of the real-time line vs. the frontier line** (same-prompt comparison)
- **Whether aggregated models' outputs are post-processed by Krea** (upscaling/filter chains)
- **The export and reuse surface of LoRA training artifacts**
unknowns:
- Upscaling ceiling (official copy mentions 22K, the fetched snapshot did not show it — not verified item by item)
- The training-terms original text and its clause-level correspondence to "Do not train" (not verified line by line)
- The API's model coverage and quotas (not verified item by item)
- Cross-session memory mechanism (no official statement verified)
related: It is right inside the aggregation surface: Krea offers an Ideogram generation entry, while Ideogram's own bench has a fuller feature surface.
It is right inside the aggregation surface: Krea runs Flux in the cloud, Flux weights can be downloaded and run locally.
Also an aggregation relationship: Krea's video line aggregates Veo; see the Veo dossier for the model itself's capability boundaries.
